title: Article 174 — Sessions of the State Legislature, prorogation and dissolution

content.overview: Article 174 requires the Governor to summon the House or each House of the Legislature of the State to meet at such time and place as he thinks fit, but six months shall not intervene between its last sitting in one session and the date appointed for its first sitting in the next session. The Governor may from time to time prorogue the House or either House and dissolve the Legislative Assembly.
content.glance: Governor summons House(s) (max 6-month gap); may prorogue; may dissolve the Legislative Assembly only. Parallel to Art 85.
content.study:
Article 174 is the State counterpart of Article 85:
(1) Summon the House or each House; six-month maximum gap between sessions.
(2) Prorogue the House or either House; dissolve the Legislative Assembly (not the Legislative Council).

Examination: 6-month rule; summon / prorogue / dissolve; only Assembly is dissolved.

sections.heading: Powers
sections.body:
1. Summon House or each House (six-month maximum gap).
2. Prorogue the House or either House.
3. Dissolve the Legislative Assembly (not the Council).

questionsAndAnswers.question: Explain Article 174.
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 174 requires the Governor to summon the House or each House of the State Legislature from time to time so that not more than six months intervene between the last sitting of one session and the first sitting of the next. The Governor may prorogue the House or either House and may dissolve the Legislative Assembly. The Legislative Council is not subject to dissolution.

examTips: Parallel to Art 85; 6-month gap; dissolve Assembly only.

keyTakeaways: Art 174: summon, prorogue, dissolve Assembly; 6-month session rule.
